entries.title: The camera (K)
q: how do i film my town
how to record a video of my village
how do i make a video
entries.answer: Press K (or the Camera button at the top of the U page) to film the town with no commands. Four tabs: Orbit (round the heart, a folk or where you stand), Fly-through (a smooth flight through points you set), Follow (one folk over its shoulder through its day) and Happening (the busiest thing going on near you). Underneath: Clean shot, the lens and name tags.
steps: Pick a tab and set it up (radius, height, speed; points; a folk).
Press play. Esc always gives you your own eyes back.
tips: Use your recording software (or the game's own screenshots) to capture it: the camera moves, you record.
K over a running shot opens the screen to change it live.
warn: The camera sees only what your client has loaded: far shots show the edge of your render distance.

entries.title: Orbit shots
q: circle the town with the camera
entries.answer: Camera → Orbit circles the town's heart, the folk you were looking at when you opened the camera, or where you stand. Set the radius, height and speed (either way round, or still). It glides in from your eyes, rises over hills, and on a close orbit stops short of walls and trees.

entries.title: Fly-through shots
q: how do i make a camera path
entries.answer: Stand where the shot should pass, look where it should look, press K and Add point (two to six points). Then play: a smooth curve through every point at an even pace, easing in and out (or round and round), banking into the turns. Set how many seconds it lasts.
steps: Walk to the first spot, look the right way, press K → Fly-through → Add point.
Repeat for each point (up to six).
Set the length and once / loop, then play.

entries.title: Following a folk on camera
q: follow a villager with the camera
entries.answer: Camera → Follow films one folk over its shoulder through its day. Your favourites in reach are listed first (starred), then the folk nearest you. It swings round as the folk turns and pulls in short of walls; a folk lost from sight is circled where it was last seen.

entries.title: Show me something happening, and time-lapses
q: how do i make a timelapse
entries.answer: Happening → 'Show me something happening' takes the camera to the busiest thing near you right now: a match, music and dancing, builders at work, buying and selling, children at play, the smithy, woodcutters... Press it again for another. Time-lapse (operators, or the owner of a single-player world) runs the world 4 to 32 times faster for 5 to 60 seconds while the camera circles a building going up.
controls: [K] → Happening → Show me something happening · Time-lapse
warn: On a server, only operators may run a time-lapse: it speeds up the whole world.

entries.title: Controls while a shot runs
q: how do i stop the camera
how do i get out of the camera
entries.answer: While a shot runs: Esc stops it and gives you your own eyes back (always), Space pauses (or replays a finished fly-through), the arrow keys change speed and height, the mouse wheel the distance (the lens on a fly-through), H hides or shows the key reminder, and K opens the camera screen over the shot to change it live.
controls: [Esc] stop · [Space] pause · [←][→][↑][↓] speed & height · [Scroll] distance · [H] hints · [K] change live
tips: Your body, hand and crosshair are kept out of the picture; drop, use and swap keys do nothing while filming.

entries.title: Clean shots, the lens and name tags
entries.answer: Under every camera tab: Clean shot (on by default: no HUD, name tags or the mod's labels, like F1), the lens (20 to 100 degrees), and the folk's name tags for ordinary play: all of the tag, names only, only the folk you look at, or none, and how far they show.
controls: [F1] hides every label of the mod's
tips: By default a tag shows the name, a stuck folk's red warning and a hurt folk's health, out to 32 blocks.
The same settings are in config/mc_assistant-client.toml under [town].
